claims.text: Machine-learning potentials with active learning can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
Machine-learning potentials can learn complex relationships between atomic configurations and energies from a limited set of ab initio calculations.
Machine-learning potentials with active learning can predict free energies and entropy terms.
Active learning selectively adds training configurations that improve model accuracy and efficiency.
The proposed method applies to both solid and fluid states near phase transitions.
The proposed method will provide a 10–100-fold speedup relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will provide a 10–100-fold speedup relative to TOR-TILD.
The fidelity of the proposed method will be comparable to or better than that of TOR-TILD.
The proposed composition domain includes elemental, binary, and multicomponent systems.
The proposed temperature domain is near phase transitions under high-temperature conditions.

contradictions.description: The scope is described as 'high-entropy systems' while explicitly including elemental and binary systems, which ordinarily are not themselves multicomponent high-entropy systems.

The predicted minimum speedup is 10-fold, but the hypothesis is only falsified below 5-fold; therefore a measured 5–9-fold speedup would contradict the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
